inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,621 logical lines. The paper develops a quantum-optical realization of the Dirichlet and lowest-order Riemann–Siegel representations, then changes representation from state overlaps to Wigner magnitudes and phase-retaining Moyal functions. Material depth also includes the normalization/conservation obstruction at the Dirichlet boundary, critical-line simplifications of a tuned reference state, a smoother correction-term realization obtained by redesigning that reference state, and an appendix showing why an observable overlap can remain accurate under a poor pointwise Hamiltonian approximation. Formula extraction is mostly legible but several central displayed equations remain scan-sensitive.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, abstract, and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic framing plus the paper's headline claim that joint measurements extend a single-system Dirichlet realization into the critical strip.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Historical convergence/continuation background, operational entanglement proposal, comparison with cat-state engineering, and roadmap.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Zeta states and their properties
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines truncated and infinite zeta states, their normalization boundary, photon statistics, and logarithmic time generator.

sections_inspected.label: 3. State engineering with the Riemann zeta function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds Dirichlet and Riemann–Siegel overlaps from conditional logarithmic evolution, entanglement, and a tuned reference projection.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Riemann zeta function from Wigner phase space
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Translates the constructions into Wigner functions/matrices, separating phase-space motion, off-diagonal coherence, and magnitude-squared overlap cancellation.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Riemann zeta function described by Moyal functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Replaces real Wigner overlaps by complex Moyal functions so phase-space integration returns the complex zeta amplitude.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Conclusion and outlook; acknowledgments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Summarizes the construction, extends it to a smooth first-correction representation, and tests the necessity of a second system.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix A. Wigner representation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Supplies Moyal integral identities, Wigner-matrix information structure, and photon-number-basis formulas used in the main text.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix B. Riemann Hamiltonian from a Jaynes–Cummings model
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives an effective interaction and explains observable-level robustness to imperfect generator matching.

sections_inspected.label: References
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography only; no additional source argument.

accepted_units.title: From the Dirichlet convergence wall to the Riemann–Siegel split
accepted_units.why_material: Connects Euler-product/Dirichlet convergence to Riemann's continuation and reports Siegel's reconstruction of a saddle-point decomposition into two similar sums whose lowest-order cancellation singles out real part one-half.
accepted_units.context_note: Self-contained historical and methodological setup; its cancellation statement is explicitly about a lowest-order asymptotic representation, not a proof of the hypothesis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-supported; equations (1) and the extracted inequalities should be checked against the scan for exact notation.

accepted_units.title: Probability conservation as the single-system Dirichlet boundary
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies the core obstruction: normalization of one physical state realizes only the convergent Dirichlet domain, while a joint measurement on two interacting systems is proposed to bypass that representation limit.
accepted_units.context_note: Precedes the carried operational overview and supplies its missing reason for introducing entanglement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant and recoverable from the text layer.

accepted_units.title: Three-step joint-measurement construction and analytic-continuation analogy
accepted_units.why_material: Specifies preparation, conditional evolution, and joint projection; explains how logarithmic photon-number phases and a superposition of oppositely evolved zeta states motivate the analogy between entanglement and analytic continuation.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. Lines 134–142 are required surrounding context for the conservation obstruction this construction addresses.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; the state-engineering comparison is legible without reconstructing omitted formulas.

accepted_units.title: Zeta-state normalization inherits Dirichlet convergence
accepted_units.why_material: Defines finite and infinite photon-number zeta states and shows that normalization of the infinite state is the reciprocal of the real Dirichlet sum, so existence of the state inherits the condition that the real part exceed one.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the state and normalization setup referenced by the later Dirichlet-overlap construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent on equations (2)–(5); prose fixes the indexing and convergence conclusion, but scan verification is advisable.

accepted_units.title: Polynomial zeta weights as a logarithmic reparameterization of thermal weights
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts exponential thermal photon statistics with polynomial zeta-state statistics and isolates the substitution of photon number by its logarithm as the structural change.
accepted_units.context_note: A compact comparison that motivates the logarithmic Hamiltonian introduced immediately afterward.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (6)–(8) are legible in conjunction with the explanatory prose.

accepted_units.title: Logarithmic evolution and atom-conditioned opposite phases
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the logarithmic number Hamiltonian and its two-level conditional extension, mapping real part to initial occupation weights and imaginary part to evolution time while replacing the usual linear number coupling by a logarithm.
accepted_units.context_note: Bridges the state definition to both the single-branch Dirichlet overlap and the later two-branch Riemann–Siegel state.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent on equations (9)–(12); one extracted frequency glyph is defective, but the logarithmic dependence and conditional signs are clear.

accepted_units.title: Dirichlet zeta as a return amplitude and classical interference law
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the normalized zeta function as the overlap between initial and logarithmically evolved zeta states, then shows that the same mechanism is classical interference and interprets Dirichlet convergence as conservation of total intensity.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. Lines 239–331 are needed to supply the referenced state normalization and logarithmic generator rather than forcing their reconstruction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent on equations (13)–(14), with the physical conclusion also stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Riemann–Siegel continuation as oppositely phased truncated branches
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites the lowest-order Riemann–Siegel formula as two truncated Dirichlet-like sums with opposite logarithmic phases and relates that paired structure to atom-conditioned forward/backward evolution.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly limits this to the lowest approximation and defers corrections to section 6.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent on equations (15)–(17); Gamma, cutoff, and OCR-damaged symbols require scan verification before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Entangled branch state plus tuned reference projection produces the Riemann–Siegel amplitude
accepted_units.why_material: Constructs the equal-weight atom-field branch state, evolves it into opposite zeta phases, and chooses a parameter-dependent reference state whose overlap reproduces the two-sum Riemann–Siegel expression up to normalization.
accepted_units.context_note: The reference state's time parameter is chosen to match a particular evolved state; it is not a single time-independent readout state for all times.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent on equations (18)–(24); exact normalization factors should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: The tuned reference state disentangles on the critical line
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that although the evolved branch state is entangled, the reference state becomes a field–atom product specifically at real part one-half because its coefficient reduces to a pure phase.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a property of the chosen measurement/reference construction, not independent evidence that all nontrivial zeros lie on the line.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (25)–(26); the product-state conclusion is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Wigner and Moyal components expose state interference
accepted_units.why_material: Motivates experimentally accessible phase-space reconstruction and expands the zeta-state Wigner function into diagonal photon-number terms plus off-diagonal Moyal interference terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Appendix A supplies the underlying Wigner/Moyal identities; this unit records their application to the zeta state.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (28) is extraction-fragile and should be scan-checked; the diagonal/off-diagonal decomposition is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Logarithmic phase shear breaks and curls the Wigner wedge
accepted_units.why_material: Explains phase-space deformation through a velocity inversely proportional to photon number: low-index components move faster, causing a wedge to shear, curl, and develop interference negativity.
accepted_units.context_note: Figure 1 illustrates rather than solely establishes the mechanism; equations and prose provide the causal account.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Partly figure-dependent; the velocity law in equation (29) and descriptive prose remain recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Wigner overlap retains only the zeta magnitude squared
accepted_units.why_material: Maps the return probability to an integral of the initial and evolved Wigner functions, making phase-space cancellation compute the normalized absolute square rather than the complex zeta value.
accepted_units.context_note: This limitation directly motivates the later move to Moyal functions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equation (30) and figure 2; the magnitude-only conclusion is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Wigner matrices retain diagonal branches and off-diagonal coherence
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the Wigner matrix of a bipartite state and separates branch Wigner functions from cross-branch Moyal functions, preparing a phase-space account of entanglement and overlap.
accepted_units.context_note: This is required setup for the carried Riemann–Siegel Wigner-matrix unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent on equation (31), whose operator labels are sufficiently legible but should be scan-checked for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Opposite branch rotation and stationary off-diagonal interference
accepted_units.why_material: Analyzes the Riemann–Siegel Wigner matrix: diagonal branch functions rotate in opposite directions and shear, while off-diagonal terms remain spatially unrotated and change through complex scaling, localizing a distinct role for coherence.
accepted_units.context_note: Carried unchanged from v1. Lines 620–654 supply the matrix definition, and lines 761–764 complete the final consequence about redistributed positive and negative regions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (32)–(37) and figures 3–4 are formula/image dependent; prose supports the rotation-versus-scaling distinction.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line product structure makes every reference Wigner-matrix entry share one shape
accepted_units.why_material: Tracks how the tuned reference state's diagonal and off-diagonal components vary with real part, then shows that at one-half all entries reduce to the same Wigner shape scaled only by constants and conjugate phases.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines the general reference matrix with its critical-line reduction; numerical figure remarks are illustrative.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (38)–(39) and figure 5; exact scaling notation is scan-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: A Wigner-matrix overlap kernel turns a zero into signed phase-space cancellation
accepted_units.why_material: Expresses the Riemann–Siegel return probability through a kernel containing diagonal and off-diagonal products, and interprets small values near a chosen zero as cancellation of positive and negative phase-space regions.
accepted_units.context_note: The computation uses a truncated, lowest-order formula; its nonzero residue and off-line comparison do not prove the Riemann hypothesis.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (40)–(41), figure 6, and table 1 carry quantitative details and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Moyal integration restores the complex scalar product lost by Wigner overlap
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the complex cross-state Moyal function whose phase-space integral returns a scalar product including phase, resolving the Wigner representation's magnitude-only limitation.
accepted_units.context_note: General mechanism first, followed by separate applications to the Dirichlet and Riemann–Siegel constructions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent on equations (42)–(43), with the purpose clearly stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Dirichlet zeta as an integral of a complex zeta-state Moyal function
accepted_units.why_material: Applies the Moyal identity to the initial/evolved zeta-state pair so a complex phase-space distribution integrates to the normalized complex zeta value, and contrasts its dynamics with the Wigner function.
accepted_units.context_note: The tabular interlude at lines 934–951 belongs to the preceding Wigner calculation but does not break the stated Moyal derivation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (44) and figure 7 are scan/image dependent; the complex-versus-real distinction is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: A sum of branch Moyal functions represents the complex Riemann–Siegel value
accepted_units.why_material: Recasts the two weighted branch overlaps as a sum of cross-state Moyal functions whose integral yields the complex Riemann–Siegel approximation, and records the exceptional symmetry of its magnitude at real part one-half.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a cross-state Moyal sum, not itself the Wigner operator matrix of the entangled state.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly dependent on equations (45)–(46) and figure 8; exact exponents and normalization need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A smoother first correction is implemented by redesigning the reference state
accepted_units.why_material: Moves beyond the discontinuous lowest-order Riemann–Siegel truncation to a complementary-error-function representation and shows that the first correction can be incorporated by changing the reference state while retaining the evolved branch state.
accepted_units.context_note: The complete correction formula is quoted rather than derived; the constructive contribution is the changed projection state and its overlap.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent on equations (47)–(48) and OCR-damaged special-function notation; scan verification is required for exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Why a single-system phase-conjugate revival does not remove the two-system requirement
accepted_units.why_material: Tests the construction against a particle-in-a-box counterexample and argues that its conjugate superposition is already encoded by periodic boundary-induced initial conditions rather than generated from one generic system's evolution.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a source-stated physical argument, not a general impossibility theorem over all single-system dynamics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-only and recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Moyal functions turn cross-state operators into scalar products and overlap products
accepted_units.why_material: Defines cross-state Moyal functions, establishes conjugation and normalization identities, and derives the phase-space product identity whose equal-state specialization gives ordinary Wigner normalization and fidelity.
accepted_units.context_note: General appendix machinery supporting both main-text representation changes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-dependent on equations (A.1)–(A.5); extracted bra-ket placement should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Off-diagonal Wigner-matrix entries carry entanglement information erased by partial trace
accepted_units.why_material: Generalizes Moyal integration to bipartite scalar products, shows that tracing out a subsystem retains only diagonal Wigner entries, and identifies off-diagonal entries as the entanglement-bearing contributions that still enter full-state overlaps.
accepted_units.context_note: Provides the information-theoretic interpretation behind the main text's diagonal/off-diagonal split.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (A.6)–(A.9); prose makes the trace and off-diagonal conclusions explicit.

accepted_units.title: Photon-number expansions separate populations from interference Moyal terms
accepted_units.why_material: Expands arbitrary single-system and bipartite states in the photon-number basis and decomposes their Wigner objects into diagonal population terms and off-diagonal interference terms, supplying the reusable calculation behind the paper's phase-space formulas.
accepted_units.context_note: The special-function kernel is technical support, but the population/interference decomposition is materially reused throughout the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strongly formula-dependent on equation (A.10) and subsequent sums; Laguerre indices and conjugations are scan-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Accurate overlap can survive an inaccurate pointwise Hamiltonian approximation
accepted_units.why_material: Derives a second-order effective Jaynes–Cummings-like generator and explains three reasons its aggregate zeta overlap can be accurate without matching each logarithmic phase: phases need only agree modulo a cycle, high-index errors are downweighted, and summed errors can compensate.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument concerns the output overlap for a chosen weighted state, not operator-norm accuracy of the Hamiltonian.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (B.1)–(B.3) are extraction-fragile; the three robustness mechanisms are explicitly enumerated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Polynomial coupling reduces logarithmic simulation to coefficient optimization
accepted_units.why_material: Restricts the field coupling to an even polynomial, gives a small illustrative coefficient choice, and shows output-level agreement despite poor exponent matching, while correctly leaving systematic optimization unresolved.
accepted_units.context_note: The plotted parameter example is evidence for feasibility only and is not a convergence or error bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equations (B.4)–(B.7) and figure B.1; exact numerical claims are figure-dependent.

v1_context_repairs.reason: The carried overlap unit invokes the zeta state, its normalization, and the logarithmic Hamiltonian without defining them; the expanded interval supplies that exact setup.
The carried overview begins with operational steps but omits the immediately preceding probability-conservation obstruction that explains why a joint two-system construction is introduced.
The carried dynamics unit needs the preceding Wigner-matrix definition and the post-span completion of its final statement about how complex scaling redistributes positive and negative regions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Convergence as physical normalizability and intensity conservation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same Dirichlet boundary appears first as normalizability of an infinite state and again as conservation of total intensity in a classical interferometer, making convergence a representation-resource constraint rather than a merely formal condition.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is an analogy for this realization; it does not show that analytic continuation generally requires nonclassical resources.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic continuation by coherent branch synthesis and selective projection
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source's continuation mechanism decomposes a target into oppositely phased finite branches, stores them coherently in a bipartite state, and recombines them through a tuned projection whose off-diagonal phase-space terms preserve cross-branch information.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Only a particular lowest-order Riemann–Siegel representation is realized, with a target-parameter-dependent reference state.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Magnitude and phase form a hierarchy of phase-space representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Real Wigner overlaps expose signed cancellation but return magnitude squared, whereas cross-state Moyal functions retain relative phase and integrate to the complex amplitude for both single-branch and entangled constructions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The phase-space pictures are representational diagnostics, not an independent analytic continuation or zero-finding proof.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Critical-line simplification links product reference states, symmetry, and cancellation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: At real part one-half the chosen reference disentangles, its Wigner-matrix entries share one symmetric shape, and the resulting overlap kernel admits especially transparent signed cancellation near a sampled zero.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These properties depend on the engineered reference and truncated approximation and do not establish that all nontrivial zeros lie on the line.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Correction terms can be moved from dynamics into measurement design
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The branch dynamics used for the lowest-order formula can be retained while a smoother first correction is incorporated by changing the reference-state weights, illustrating a dynamics-versus-readout design tradeoff.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source treats one quoted correction representation and does not prove a general compilation principle.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Observable accuracy need not track generator accuracy
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Weighted overlap observables can tolerate large pointwise spectral errors because phases are periodic, high-index contributions are suppressed, and errors can cancel in the sum; this permits low-degree effective couplings to approximate the output before the Hamiltonian itself is close.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The numerical example supplies no uniform error bound and leaves coefficient optimization open.

within_source_saturation: Saturated after inspecting every logical line: all distinct mechanisms, representation changes, obstructions, correction logic, and approximation arguments are selected; unselected prose is roadmap/summary, page furniture, acknowledgments, or bibliography, while technical formula support is either included with its parent mechanism or explicitly marked scan-sensitive.
stop_reason: The source ends after the effective-Hamiltonian feasibility argument and bibliography. Further segmentation would split already represented derivations into routine algebra, duplicate figure narration, or select reference metadata rather than add a new semantic mechanism.
